new_scholarship.name: World in Serbia Project Scholarships of the Government of the Republic of Serbia
new_scholarship.official_source: Ministry of Education, Science and Technological Development of the Republic of Serbia
new_scholarship.description: The "World in Serbia" project is a Government of the Republic of Serbia scholarship programme run by the Ministry of Education for candidates from member and observer states of the Non-Aligned Movement, covering candidates from Africa, Asia, Central and South America. Scholarship holders study free of charge at public higher education institutions founded by the Republic of Serbia, in all study programmes and at all study levels, after a preparatory Serbian-language year. The February 2026 official call covers Serbian-language study in the 2026/2027 academic year and enrolment at Serbian higher education institutions in the 2027/2028 academic year, with applications due no later than 1 June 2026.
new_scholarship.duration: One year of Serbian-language preparation (2026/2027) followed by the enrolled degree cycle beginning in the 2027/2028 academic year
new_scholarship.deadline: No later than 1 June 2026 for the 2026 call; the call is reissued annually, so the next cycle is expected to close around the same date in 2027
new_scholarship.application_period: Serbian language study in the 2026/2027 academic year, then enrolment in higher education institutions founded by the Republic of Serbia in the 2027/2028 academic year
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Citizens of Non-Aligned Movement member or observer states, nominated by the competent authority of their country, with age limits of under 21 for first-level studies, under 25 for second-level studies and under 35 for third-level (doctoral) studies, an overall 80% pass grade at undergraduate and master level, English or Serbian at A1 level, and good health.
eligibility: Citizen of a member state or observer state of the Non-Aligned Movement
Nominated by the competent authority of the participating state in the Project
Younger than 21 years old for enrolment in first-level studies
Younger than 25 years old for second-level studies (master's, specialist and specialist vocational)
Younger than 35 years old for third-level studies (doctoral)
Overall pass grade of at least 80% at undergraduate and master level
Knowledge of English at least at A1 level, or Serbian at least at A1 level on arrival
In overall good health, verified by the Student Health Care Institute of Belgrade
coverage: Free tuition at higher education institutions founded by the Republic of Serbia
Accommodation and meals in the student standard (student centre) system
benefits: Free of charge study (tuition) at all study programmes and levels at institutions founded by the Republic of Serbia
Accommodation and food in the student standard system of the Republic of Serbia (Belgrade, Novi Sad, Nis, Kragujevac)
Financial scholarship of RSD 18,000 per month
Health insurance
Free intensive Serbian-language courses before enrolment
Assistance with translation and recognition of prior diplomas by the Ministry of Education and the Qualifications Agency
requirements: Pass the Serbian language examination before commencing higher education studies
Pass the entrance exam at the chosen faculty and complete enrolment
Earn a minimum of 37 ECTS credits during the academic year for budget-funded re-enrolment
Regularly attend classes and sit the prescribed examinations
Obtain and maintain temporary residence status in the Republic of Serbia
Inform the Ministry of Education of material changes to scholarship status within 30 days
Return to the country that nominated them upon completion of studies
required_documents: Curriculum vitae with a motivational letter
Copy of the travel document (passport), valid for at least another 6 years at the date of submission for a visa
Proof of acquired education (certified transcripts, secondary school certificates, diplomas, grade transcripts, diploma supplements) translated into Serbian or English
Health documentation, subject to a general medical examination on arrival
Completed and signed application form, submitted to the relevant institution in the candidate's country for endorsement
application_method: Submit the completed application form through the official Google Form link given in the call
Email scanned original documentation plus Serbian or English certified translations to worldinserbia@prosveta.gov.rs
A copy of the documentation and the health certificate is submitted to the relevant institution in the candidate's country for formal endorsement
The endorsing institution submits the list of endorsed candidates to the Serbian diplomatic-consular mission, which forwards it via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
new_scholarship.english_requirement: English at A1 level accepted as an alternative to Serbian; all documentation must be translated into English or Serbian
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Each participating state must nominate endorsed candidates. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs transmits the lists of nominated candidates with all application forms to the Ministry of Education no later than 10 June. A special inter-ministerial commission comprising representatives of the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Agency for Qualifications (ENIC/NARIC Centre) and the Student Health Care Institute of Belgrade selects the candidates, and the decision on the final list of endorsed candidates is adopted by the Minister responsible for education no later than 26 June. Scholarships may be terminated for inauthentic or fraudulent documentation, unverified health documentation, failure to pass the Serbian language examination, failure to obtain the required ECTS credits, or voluntary renunciation.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Students from Non-Aligned Movement countries in Africa, Asia and Central and South America who can obtain a government endorsement and are willing to study in Serbian after a preparatory language year.
new_scholarship.notes: The published February 2026 call states a monthly financial scholarship of RSD 18,000. Approximately 536 scholarship holders from 127 countries were studying in Serbia under the project at the time of publication.

new_scholarship.name: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship funds one-year Honours or two-year Master's study in any field at a recognised South African institution for young African leaders aged 19 to 29, and pairs it with a compulsory leadership development programme of residential workshops. It covers tuition and registration fees, study materials, research, medical aid, accommodation and meals, a personal allowance and economy-class flights for international scholars. Applications for the 2027 intake closed on 14 April 2026 and applications for the Class of 2028 open on 9 March 2027, closing 14 April 2027.
new_scholarship.duration: Maximum two years of funding: one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Master's degree
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications for 2028 open 9 March 2027 and close 23:59 GMT+2 on Wednesday 14 April 2027; no late or incomplete applications are accepted
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications for the Class of 2028 open 9 March 2027 and close on 14 April 2027; shortlisted candidates are notified by mid-July, interviews take place in October, and scholars must secure university admission and a study visa by January 2028
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Citizens of any African country aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, able to study at postgraduate level in English, holding or completing an undergraduate degree with above 70% or upper-second-class results by 1 January 2028, and committed to the Foundation's principles of leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship.

Aspire to ethical leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship and agree to reflect on personal growth
Willing to participate fully in the compulsory leadership development programme
Not permitted to hold other scholarships or funded opportunities concurrently
coverage: Tuition and registration fees at a recognised South African institution

new_scholarship.english_requirement: Yes: applicants must be able to do written and verbal academic work in English at postgraduate level, as English is the main medium of tuition at South African universities, and all documents and transcripts must be in English
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection runs in rounds: document review, then notification by mid-July for round two, notification by end of July for round three, notification by end of August for the final interview round, in-person interviews in South Africa in October for candidates based outside South Africa, and final selection notified by the end of October. Selection is based on academic strength (above 70% or upper second) and demonstrated leadership, and on the character of leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship sought by the Foundation. Candidates who do not agree with one or more character statements are warned but may still apply.
new_scholarship.best_fit: African citizens aged 19 to 29 with excellent undergraduate results who want a funded postgraduate degree in South Africa combined with a structured leadership programme and mentorship network.
new_scholarship.notes: The Foundation funds a strict maximum of two years. MBAs, block courses and courses delivered predominantly online are not funded, distance learning is not allowed, and undergraduate study is not funded.

new_scholarship.name: Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship for Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam (BDGS)
new_scholarship.official_source: Government of Brunei Darussalam, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Education
new_scholarship.description: The Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship for Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam, known as BDGS, is the Government of Brunei Darussalam's scholarship scheme for international applicants, administered by the Ministry of Education with applications handled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs through its Katalyst applicant portal. It covers undergraduate and postgraduate study at institutions in Brunei Darussalam, with tuition paid by the government plus bursaries for accommodation, books, food and personal spending, complementary medical treatment in Brunei government hospitals and travel arranged through Brunei's diplomatic missions. The applicant portal for the 2026/2027 session now displays that applications are closed, and the scheme is announced annually.

new_scholarship.name: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS)
new_scholarship.official_source: Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, Republic of Mauritius
new_scholarship.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 edition funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, paying tuition and course-related costs up to a published cap, a monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 and a return airfare, while requiring awardees to have already secured or applied for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution. Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.
new_scholarship.duration: Diploma up to three years, Bachelor's up to four years, MPhil up to two years plus six months for thesis defence, MPhil/PhD up to three years plus six months for the transfer report plus one year plus six months for the thesis defence, PhD up to three years plus six months
new_scholarship.deadline: No central date is published: each nominating agency sets its own deadline and communicates it to prospective applicants. For the 2026 edition the Mauritian public universities opened their own application windows from October 2025 and closed them between February and March 2026, so the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
new_scholarship.application_period: Annual edition published by the Ministry, with applications made through the nominating agency in the applicant's country and in parallel with the chosen Mauritian public university's admission window
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Resident citizens of African Union member states or African Commonwealth countries aged between 18 and 26 for undergraduate programmes or under 40 for MPhil and PhD programmes by 1 January of the intake year, with a qualifying secondary or undergraduate result of about 60% or 12/20 or the equivalent, and holding or applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public higher education institution.

Not already hold an undergraduate degree when applying for an undergraduate programme
Not be a self-financing African student already studying in Mauritius applying for the same programme level

Return airfare by the most economical route to and from Mauritius

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is on merit, after all attached conditions are satisfied and the host institution confirms a seat has been offered. Applications without endorsement from a nominating agency, or from the Ministry of Education where no agency exists, are not considered. Candidates not informed of selection within six months of the application deadline should consider themselves not selected, and the Ministry does not respond to individual queries. The final and binding decision on award rests with the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, and the Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call.

new_scholarship.description: The Ghana Education Trust Fund's postgraduate foreign scholarship supports Ghanaians studying at postgraduate level outside Ghana, with financial support covering tuition fees, accommodation and scholastic materials. GETFund describes its programme as financial, social and academic support with priority given to STEM programmes and to female education, and it also funds capacity building, faculty development through the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission and short courses abroad. Applications for the 2026/2027 postgraduate foreign scholarships opened on 13 April 2026 and closed on 30 April 2026, so the next round is expected in the first half of 2027.
